Stated Claim / Post Context:
Thread Reader — unroll any X thread, free

Free thread reader for X (Twitter). Paste a link to any post in a thread and read the whole thing as one page: images, quotes, links. Copy as text or Markdown.

Actual Article Body:
Paste a link to any post in a thread. The reader finds the first one, follows the author's replies in order and shows the whole thread as an article: images, quoted posts and links included. Copy it as text or Markdown when you are done.

Any post in the thread works; we find the first one. Public threads only, no login.

Open the thread on X and copy the link to any post in it, the first, the one that went viral, or the last. Tap Share, then Copy link.

Paste it above and press Unroll. We walk up to the first post, then read the author's follow-ups in order. Ten to thirty seconds for a long thread.

Read it as one page: numbered posts, images and video stills, quoted posts, links kept clickable, and the like and view counts per post.

Copy the thread as plain text or Markdown, copy a reader link to share, or turn the first post into a clean screenshot with the tweet generator.

The classic Thread Reader App worked by replying @threadreaderapp unroll under a thread and waiting for a link. It depended on X's API, which got expensive in 2023, and the bot has been unreliable since. Half the threads people want to read today are older than the last time it answered.

This reader does not tag anything. It reads the thread the way a logged-out browser does, from any post in it, and gives you the page in seconds. Nothing is posted under the thread, so the author never sees a bot reply.

We built it for our own work: turning a thread that landed into an X Article starts with the thread as text, and the MCP does the rest.

What is a thread reader?

A thread reader takes an X (Twitter) thread, which the platform shows as a chain of separate posts with replies between them, and unrolls it into one continuous page in order. You paste a link, it finds the first post, follows the author's own replies and shows them as a single article with the images, quotes and links kept.

What happened to the Thread Reader App and the @threadreaderapp unroll bot?

The original Thread Reader App and its 'unroll' reply bot ran on X's API. After the 2023 API pricing changes, third-party access became expensive and unreliable, and the reply bot stopped working for most people. This reader does not depend on the reply bot: you paste a link into the page instead of tagging an account under the thread.
